**ai-teammate** (2026-09-24):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: budgets seeded on local hardware, enforced on `runner-pick` hardware — including the slow hosted fallback this issue is about**

These six budgets were measured on a local no-key M-class arm64 machine (+20% headroom, +10% gate tolerance ⇒ ~+32% effective). The gate consumes runs on `fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration)`: self-hosted fa-m5 minis **or the hosted-ubuntu fallback** — and issue #928's motivating data point is precisely that the hosted fallback is slow (41.9 min leg wall). Process-spawn/PTY-heavy suites (all six budgeted suites are spawn-heavy: `dap_*`, `poisoned_provider_boot`, `headless_tools_flag`, `trajectory/*`) are exactly where hosted-vs-local deltas exceed 30%.

When the fallback path trips the gate, the only remedies are "shave or re-shard" (not actionable if the suite didn't change) or a hand-edited raise in a reviewed PR — i.e. a persistently red critical-path gate on PRs that touched nothing relevant.

Suggestions:
1. After the first SM-started CI run on this branch (already promised in the description), re-seed these six entries from the CI `integration-json-shard-*` artifacts rather than the local run — one `--update-baseline` reviewed PR.
2. Consider pinning the seed/gate to one runner class, or noting in `_meta` which runner class the budgets assume so the next tightening PR knows what it is comparing against.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-24):

💡 **SUGGESTION: shard "balance" is nominal — 67 of 73 weights are the 100 s placeholder**

`meta.source` says it honestly: "timing (partial: no-key local seed) + 100s default for unmeasured suites". With 67/73 files at the default weight, the bin-pack balance is trivial (any split of equal weights balances), and the suspiciously perfect `estimated_load` `[3449.5, 3449.6]` (≈57.5 min/shard) is an artifact of placeholders — if those weights were real, each shard would blow the new 40-min `timeout-minutes` (real leg is ~41.9 min total, so ~21 min/shard today).

No action required for this PR (the manifest is verifiably union-complete/disjoint, and real junit lands via this very PR), but until the Part 2.2 data-driven re-shard:
- don't read `estimated_load` as a wall-time forecast (suite totals ≠ shard wall time, and the weights are guesses);
- when rebalancing, seed `weights` from the merged junit artifacts rather than re-defaulting new entries to 100 s.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-24):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `--tags` selector edge cases + no CI guard for the integration manifest's union/disjoint invariant**

Three small robustness gaps in the new selector path:

1. **Only the first tag is honored**: `required_tag=(tags[0] if tags else None)` silently drops a second `--tags` value. Either reject >1 (`ERROR: --tags supports one value`) or loop.
2. **Regex built by concatenation**: `"...['\"]" + tag + r"['\"]"` — fine for `integration`, but a tag with regex metacharacters would silently misbehave. Wrap with `re.escape(tag)`.
3. **4096-byte read window is silent**: a file whose `@Tags` sits past 4 KiB (long header/imports) would be silently dropped from the bin-pack safety net — i.e. a new integration test file that never runs and never warns. I verified all 73 current integration-tagged files match within the window and none use `@Tags(const [...])` (which the regex also would not match), so this is latent-only today — a `read()` of the whole file (test files are small) or a loud fallback would close it.

Related: `scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py` cannot validate the new manifest at all — `full_suite()` hard-codes the `/integration/` exclusion and there is no `--tags` pass-through, so the union/disjoint/no-extras invariant for `test_integration_shards.json` (verified manually for this PR) has no CI guard and will silently rot. Extending it with `--tags` (delegating to `shard_files.py`, as it already does) and wiring it into `guards` would make the manual check permanent.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-24):

💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicated dart-JSON span parser + no alarm for budgeted suites that stop running**

Two related points on the gate script:

1. **Second hand-rolled parser of the same format.** `parse_tests()` re-implements the `testStart`/`testDone` span logic of `scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py` (the docstring says "Same span logic"). The duration gate and the junit/rebalance pipeline must agree on durations forever; when someone fixes a parsing subtlety in one (e.g. retry semantics, group/hidden filtering), the other drifts. A tiny shared module (e.g. `scripts/_dart_json_spans.py` imported by both — both stay pure-stdlib) removes the drift class.

2. **A budgeted suite can silently exit the gate.** The check iterates suites *that ran*: a suite renamed, re-tagged, or dropped from the manifest keeps its dead baseline entry forever while its replacement shows up only on the "unbudgeted" visibility list — nobody is forced to act, and gated coverage quietly shrinks (the gate stays green with fewer gated suites). Cheap fix: report (and optionally fail on) baseline suites absent from the measurement:

```python
missing = sorted(set(baseline["suites"]) - set(suite_totals))
if missing:
    report.append(f"Budgeted suites NOT seen this run ({len(missing)}):")
    report.extend(f"  `{p}`" for p in missing)
```

(Not verified against the synthetic battery — the five advertised cases all behave correctly, exit codes included; this is the one blind spot I found in an otherwise solid script.)

blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 932
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/932
- **Title**: Add a test-duration budget gate + 2-shard the PTY/CLI critical path
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/928-duration-gate` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +632
- **Deletions**: -38
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:23:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T19:23:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #928 (Part 1 + Part 2.1; Part 3 and the data-driven shave are deliberately not here).

## Delivered

**Part 1 — duration budget gate (blocking from day one)**
- `scripts/check_test_durations.py` (pure stdlib, mirrors `check_cli_coverage.py`): consumes the dart test JSON file-reporter the integration legs now emit; **fails** when a suite total regresses >10% vs the baseline or a named per-test budget is breached; writes the **top-10 slowest tests into the GitHub job summary on every run** (plus unbudgeted-suite visibility). Suite total = sum of per-test spans, so sharding/concurrency changes don't move it.
- `scripts/test_duration_baseline.json` `{suites, per_test, _meta}` — seeded from a real measured no-key integration run (M-class arm64, `--tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), **+20% headroom**, only for the 6 suites that fully execute without provider keys (124s → 149s budgeted). Spawn-heavy PTY suites (blocked locally by the hardcoded `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd`, part 3.1) and all `llm` suites are **unbudgeted**: listed in every summary, gated the moment a reviewed PR budgets them.
- Ratchet is **structural**: `--update-baseline` refuses to RAISE an existing budget (exit 1), refuses sub-second env-skip totals (would poison a down-only ratchet with 0.0s floors), and **no workflow — scheduled or otherwise — ever invokes it**. `shard-rebalance.yml` / `coverage-gardener.yml` verified untouched. Budgets move only through reviewed PRs consuming the new `junit-integration*` artifacts.
- Enforcement: new **pty-coverage-gate** job (after the shards) runs the gate + the CLI coverage ratchet; `quality-gate` needs it → red-blocks the merge. The nightly leg emits the same json+junit (retention 14d) and runs the gate **check-only** on the scheduled keyed run — that artifact is what completes the unbudgeted suites' budgets.

**Part 2.1 — PTY/CLI leg sharded 2x**
- `scripts/test_integration_shards.json` (file-level, duration-balanced) + `shard_files.py --tags integration` (new flag: bin-packs uncovered *integration-tagged* files at runtime so a PR adding one never silently skips it; verified union/disjoint/no-extras for both shards). Matrix shards run `--file-reporter` + junit, upload json/junit/lcov artifacts; shard lcovs merge (union DA hits, NOT cat) before the coverage ratchet — a single shard's ratchet would false-regress.

**Before/after** — before: hosted-fallback leg wall **41.9 min** (nightly, hosted ubuntu — the case the issue cites); fa-m5 minis ~11-13 min recently (currently red on main for unrelated reasons). After: 2 parallel shards, test-phase spans split ~50/50 (estimated loads 3450s/3450s); **the first SM-started CI run on this branch supplies the real after-number** — per fleet rules this PR dispatches no CI.

## Remaining (not in this PR, per scope)
- Part 3 (product/test-harness code): `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp` unique CWD, dap hub port hygiene, explicit `--concurrency` tags, heavyweight-file splits. The `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` fix also unblocks local seeding of the remaining suites.
- Part 2.2: data-driven shave/re-shard of the top offenders once the first keyed junit artifacts land (candidates already named in the issue).

## Self-check evidence
- Gate script: 5-case synthetic battery (OK / suite-regression / per-test / update-lowers+adds / update-refuses-raise) all as expected, exit codes verified; run against the real 263-test/64-suite seed json → RESULT OK, exit 0.
- Ratchet poison guard: `--update-baseline` over the raw seed json budgets 15 meaningful suites and skips 58 sub-second env-skips (verified, no 0.0 floors land).
- Shard selector: both shards dry-run disjoint, union == manifest (73 files), zero bin-pack warnings, all targets exist.
- YAML: all touched workflows parse; `quality-gate`/`watchdog` needs-edges preserved.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--tags TAG (issue #928, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out


def file_has_tag(path: str, tag: str) -> bool:
    """True when the file's @Tags([...]) annotation names `tag`."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            head = f.read(4096)
    except OSError:
        return False
    return re.search(r"@Tags\s*\(\s*\[[^\]]*['\"]" + tag + r"['\"]", head) is not None


def uncovered_files(covered: set, root: str, exclude: list,
                    required_tag=None) -> list:
    """Individual test files missing from a file-level manifest, as (path, 1).

    Default (no required_tag): files under test/ excluding integration and
    --exclude matches — the core/faui manifests. With required_tag (e.g.
    the integration shards, issue #928): only files whose @Tags annotation
    names the tag — an integration manifest must never bin-pack untagged
    core files (they would be filtered out by --tags anyway, but selecting
    them is noise) and must NOT skip test/integration.
    """
    out = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if required_tag is None:
            if "/integration/" in norm:
                continue  # integration runs in its own CI job; excludes stay out
        elif not file_has_tag(path, required_tag):
            continue
        if norm not in covered:
            out.append((norm, 1))
    return out


def bin_pack_by_count(units: list, n: int) -> list:
    buckets = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    loads = [0] * n
    for unit, count in sorted(units, key=lambda u: -u[1]):
        i = loads.index(min(loads))
        buckets[i].append(unit)
        loads[i] += count
    return buckets


def main() -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    exclude = []
    tags = []
    while "--exclude" in argv or "--tags" in argv:
        for flag, sink in (("--exclude", exclude), ("--tags", tags)):
            while flag in argv:
                i = argv.index(flag)
                try:
                    sink.append(argv[i + 1])
                except IndexError:
                    print(f"ERROR: {flag} needs a value", file=sys.stderr)
                    return 2
                del argv[i:i + 2]
    if len(argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    manifest_path, index_s = argv
    try:
        with open(manifest_path) as f:
            manifest = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        print(f"ERROR: cannot read manifest {manifest_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:
        index = int(index_s)
        shards = manifest["shards"]
        shard = shards[index]
    except (ValueError, KeyError, IndexError):
        print(f"ERROR: no shard with index {index_s} in {manifest_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    # Loose root files expand via glob below, so only directory units can
    # go stale; anything new under test/ runs THIS PR, not next rebalance.
    covered = {u for s in shards for u in s}
    file_level = any(u.replace(os.sep, "/").endswith("_test.dart")
                     for s in shards for u in s)
    if file_level:
        # File-level manifest (issue #283): bin-pack uncovered FILES.
        extra = uncovered_files(covered, "test", exclude,
                                required_tag=(tags[0] if tags else None))
    else:
        extra = uncovered_units(covered, "test")
    if extra:
        print(
            "WARNING: test dirs missing from the manifest (new since the "
            f"last rebalance?): {[u for u, _ in extra]}; bin-packing by "
            "file count at runtime",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    extra_bucket = bin_pack_by_count(extra, len(shards))[index]

    for unit in list(shard) + extra_bucket:
        if os.path.isdir(unit):
            if os.path.normpath(unit) == "test":
                # Loose root files only — never the directory itself.
                for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(unit, "*_test.dart"))):
                    print(f.replace(os.sep, "/"))
            else:
                print(unit)
        elif os.path.isfile(unit):
            print(unit)
        else:
            print(f"WARNING: shard unit not found: {unit}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CLI-surface coverage ratchet for the PTY/terminal integration suites
(issue #177 follow-up: automatically growing terminal-test coverage).

Measures LINE coverage of lib/src/cli/** from an lcov file produced by the
integration suites (mock-endpoint PTY tests + live providers that self-skip)
and compares it against the committed baseline
(scripts/cli_coverage_baseline.txt). The baseline only ever moves UP — the
weekly coverage-gardener.yml workflow measures and bumps it, so terminal-test
coverage of the CLI surface can never silently regress.

Usage:
  check_cli_coverage.py [--lcov coverage/lcov.info] [--min-from BASELINE_FILE]
  check_cli_coverage.py --print   # just print the measured percentage
Exit 1 when below baseline.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

PREFIXES = ("SF:", "DA:")


def cli_line_coverage(lcov_path: str, scope: str = "lib/src/cli/") -> float:
    total = 0
    hit = 0
    current_in_scope = False
    with open(lcov_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                path = line[3:]
                # lcov paths may be absolute or repo-relative.
                idx = path.find(scope)
                current_in_scope = idx != -1
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current_in_scope:
                try:
                    _lineno, hits = line[3:].split(",")[:2]
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                total += 1
                if int(hits) > 0:
                    hit += 1
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return 100.0 * hit / total


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="coverage/lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--baseline",
        default=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "cli_coverage_baseline.txt"),
    )
    ap.add_argument("--print", dest="only_print", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    pct = cli_line_coverage(args.lcov)
    print(f"CLI surface coverage (lib/src/cli/**): {pct:.2f}%")
    if args.only_print:
        return 0

    baseline = 0.0
    if os.path.exists(args.baseline):
        with open(args.baseline, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            baseline = float(fh.read().strip() or "0")
    print(f"Baseline: {baseline:.2f}% (ratchet: only up)")
    if pct + 1e-9 < baseline:
        print(
            f"FAIL: CLI coverage {pct:.2f}% regressed below baseline {baseline:.2f}%.\n"
            "Add terminal/PTY tests for the uncovered CLI paths — the baseline only goes up."
        )
        return 1
    print("OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert a dart test JSON report to JUnit XML (issue #194, AC3).

`dart test` has no built-in junit reporter, so CI emits the built-in
`json:` file-reporter per shard and this converts it:

    dart test --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-0.json" ...
    python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
        test-results/dart-shard-0.json test-results/junit-shard-0.xml

The resulting junit-shard-N.xml artifacts are what
.github/workflows/shard-rebalance.yml consumes for duration-based shard
rebalancing (scripts/rebalance_shards.py --from-junit): `classname` is the
suite path, which is what the rebalancer matches units by.

Only real tests are emitted: groups arrive as "group" events (never
testStart), and the "loading <file>" pseudo-test is filtered by its hidden
testDone — so group durations never double-count their children.
Durations are seconds (dart reports ms since runner start; paired
testStart/testDone give each test's real span).

Pure stdlib.
"""

import json
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from xml.sax.saxutils import escape


def convert(json_path: str, xml_path: str) -> int:
    suites = {}  # suiteID -> test file path
    starts = {}  # testID -> (name, suite path, start ms)
    cases = []   # (name, suite path, duration_seconds, failed)
    with open(json_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                ev = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue  # torn/partial line — never fatal for timing data
            kind = ev.get("type")
            if kind == "suite":
                suites[ev["suite"]["id"]] = ev["suite"]["path"]
            elif kind == "testStart":
                starts[ev["test"]["id"]] = (
                    ev["test"].get("name", ""),
                    suites.get(ev["test"]["suiteID"], ""),
                    ev["time"],
                )
            elif kind == "testDone":
                tid = ev["testID"]
                if tid in starts and not ev.get("hidden", False):
                    name, path, t0 = starts.pop(tid)
                    dur = max((ev["time"] - t0) / 1000.0, 0.0)
                    failed = ev.get("result") in ("failure", "error")
                    cases.append((name, path, dur, failed))
    suite = ET.Element("testsuite", {
        "name": json_path,
        "tests": str(len(cases)),
    })
    for name, path, dur, failed in cases:
        tc = ET.SubElement(suite, "testcase",
                           {"name": escape(name), "classname": path,
                            "time": f"{dur:.3f}"})
        if failed:
            ET.SubElement(tc, "failure")
    tree = ET.ElementTree(suite)
    tree.write(xml_path, encoding="utf-8", xml_declaration=True)
    print(f"{xml_path}: {len(cases)} testcases")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(2)
    sys.exit(convert(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]))

blocks.text:
quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, pty-integration, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ     = ${{ needs.pty-integration.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_INTEG: ${{ needs.pty-integration.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || fail "changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || fail "supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || fail "dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          # The remaining legs are path-gated (flutter-analyze covers the
          # lib/bin/test surface; the build-* legs cover platform targets):
          # success or skipped is fine, anything else fails. Branch
          # protection relies on THIS aggregate as the single required
          # check (AGENTS.md "one aggregate Quality gate"), so every needs
          # leg must land here — a red platform build must never yield a
          # green required check.
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "pty-integration:$R_PTY_INTEG" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              fail "a leg is $r ($name)"
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.

blocks.text:
# Runner split (2026-09-22): PURE-DART jobs -> ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo:
# free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64 queue). Flutter jobs stay x64 —
# Flutter ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable 3.47.5 manifest is x64
# only; subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64').
# cube-kernel-live -> self-hosted M5 (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent).
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they…

The `needs` list includes `pty-coverage-gate` but the verification loop doesn't check `needs.pty-coverage-gate.result`.

Since quality-gate has `if: always()`, when pty-coverage-gate fails (e.g. duration budget breach), the quality-gate job would still run — and with pty-coverage-gate missing from the check list, the gate would report OK!

Wait, but does it matter? With `if: always()`, quality-gate runs regardless. Its result depends ONLY on the checks in that script. Since R_PTY_COVERAGE is not checked, a failing duration gate does NOT red-block the merge. The PR's core claim — "pty-coverage-gate ... quality-gate needs it → red-blocks the merge" — is NOT actually wired: adding a job to `needs` without adding it to the result-check loop does nothing (needs only orders/starts jobs; with `if: always()`, results are only advisory unless checked).

Hold on — is that right? In GitHub Actions, `needs` with `if: always()` — the quality-gate runs always. Its conclusion is determined by its steps. The step's script only fails on the listed legs. pty-coverage-gate result isn't listed → a failing pty-coverage-gate leaves quality-gate green. === watchdog/step-timings ===
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos]
    if: always()
    permissions:

  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).

    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23): they are
    # the two longest legs (60/45 min, macOS) and without being in `needs`
    # the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner timeout on
    # either would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi

import glob, json, os, re

man = json.load(open('scripts/test_integration_shards.json'))
shards = man['shards']
weights = man['meta']['weights']
print("estimated_load:", man['meta']['estimated_load'])
for i, s in enumerate(shards):

# disjoint + exist
allf = [f for s in shards for f in s]
dupes = {f for f in allf if allf.count(f) > 1}
print("dupes:", dupes or "none")
missing = [f for f in allf if not os.path.isfile(f)]
print("missing files:", missing or "none")

TAG_RE = re.compile(r"@Tags\s*\(\s*\[[^\]]*['\"]integration['\"]")
def has_tag(path, limit=4096):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            head = f.read(limit)
    except OSError:
        return False
    return TAG_RE.search(head) is not None

# all integration-tagged test files on disk
tagged = []
for p in sorted(glob.glob('test/**/*_test.dart', recursive=True)):
    if any(x in p for x in ('browser_ext',)):
        continue
    if has_tag(p):
        tagged.append(p)
union = set(allf)
print(f"\nmanifest union: {len(union)}, integration-tagged files on disk: {len(tagged)}")
not_in_manifest = [t for t in tagged if t not in union]
print("integration-tagged NOT in manifest (bin-pack would pick up):", not_in_manifest or "none")
no_tag_in_manifest = [f for f in allf if not has_tag(f)]
print("manifest files WITHOUT integration tag (run zero tests):", no_tag_in_manifest or "none")

# 4096-byte window risk: any integration tag beyond 4096 bytes?
risky = []
for p in tagged:
    full = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
    if not TAG_RE.search(full[:4096]) and TAG_RE.search(full):
        risky.append(p)
# also any file whose full text has the tag but head doesn't (missed by selector entirely)
for p in sorted(glob.glob('test/**/*_test.dart', recursive=True)):
    full = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
    if TAG_RE.search(full) and not has_tag(p):
        if p not in risky:
            risky.append(p)
print("files where tag sits beyond 4096B (selector misses them):", risky or "none")

# @Tags(const [...]) style anywhere?
const_style = [p for p in glob.glob('test/**/*_test.dart', recursive=True)
               if re.search(r"@Tags\s*\(\s*const\b", open(p, encoding='utf-8').read(4096))]
print("@Tags(const [...]) style files:", const_style or "none")
EOF"}

The gate script's core behaviors work as advertised: OK/regression/per-test/update-lowers+adds/refuses-raise/sub-second-skip all behave. Exit codes correct. Note the `_meta` of my synthetic baseline got overwritten by the script's meta — in the real baseline, `existing_meta` is merged (`{**existing_meta, **meta}`), so the real `_meta` (issue 928, seed_policy etc.) is preserved. Good.

One subtle observation from run 5 ("refuses to RAISE"): the refusal path still REWRITES the baseline file ("baseline written") — that's fine, it's a no-op content-wise for the refused suite (lowers/adds still apply). Good.

Now remaining checks:

1. **nightly junit-vs-json artifact mismatch**: nightly uploads ONLY junit XML, but `check_test_durations.py --update-baseline` consumes DART JSON. The PR description says "The nightly leg emits the same json+junit (retention 14d)" and "that artifact is what completes the unbudgeted suites' budgets". The diff shows only `junit-integration.xml` uploaded — NOT the raw dart json `integration.json`. Let me re-verify the nightly hunk in the full diff... From the diff:

```
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
+        if: always()
+        with:
+          name: junit-integration
+          path: test-results/junit-integration.xml
+          retention-days: 14
```

Only junit. So the nightly keyed run — the run that measures the llm suites (currently unbudgeted) — produces the raw dart json locally (test-results/integration.json) but never uploads it. A future budgeting PR cannot consume the nightly artifact with the updater (it parses dart json, not junit). The llm suites can only be budgeted from a keyed PR-shard run (integration-json-shard-* retention 2 days), which DOES upload raw json. Hmm — actually, are the provider keys present on PR runs? The env block sets OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc. from secrets on the PR leg; same-repo PRs get them (forks don't). So a same-repo PR shard run is keyed and uploads the raw json. Then the nightly is a secondary measurement. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if "/integration/" in norm or any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        out.add(norm)
    return out


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Assert shard-manifest union/disjointness/no-leak.")
    ap.add_argument("manifest")
    ap.add_argument("--shards", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--root", default="test")
    ap.add_argument("--exclude", action="append", default=[])
    args = ap.parse_args()

    shard_files_py = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                                  "shard_files.py")
    selections = []
    for i in range(args.shards):
        cmd = [sys.executable, shard_files_py, args.manifest, str(i)]
        for x in args.exclude:
            cmd += ["--exclude", x]
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            print(f"::error::shard_files.py failed for shard {i}:\n{proc.stderr}",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        selections.append({ln.strip() for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines() if ln.strip()})

    ok = True
    full = full_suite(args.root, args.exclude)
    union = set().union(*selections) if selections else set()

    missing = sorted(full - union)
    unexpected = sorted(union - full)
    if missing:
        ok = False
        print(f"::error::shard manifest misses {len(missing)} test file(s): {missing}",
              file=sys.stderr)
    if unexpected:
        ok = False
        print(f"::error::shard manifest selects {len(unexpected)} file(s) outside the "
              f"suite (stale or excluded): {unexpected}", file=sys.stderr)

    for i in range(len(selections)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(selections)):
            overlap = sorted(selections[i] & selections[j])
            if overlap:
                ok = False
                print(f"::error::shards {i} and {j} overlap on {len(overlap)} file(s): "
                      f"{overlap}", file=sys.stderr)

    leaks = sorted(f for f in union if any(x in f for x in args.exclude))
    if leaks:
        ok = False
        print(f"::error::excluded file(s) leaked into shards "
              f"({args.exclude}): {leaks}", file=sys.stderr)

    if not ok:
        return 1
    counts = ", ".join(f"shard{i}={len(s)}" for i, s in enumerate(selections))
    print(f"Shard manifest OK: union={len(union)} files == full suite, "
          f"pairwise disjoint, no excluded leaks ({counts})")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `--tags` selector edge cases + no CI guard for the integration manifest's union/disjoint invariant**

Three small robustness gaps in the new selector path:

1. **Only the first tag is honored**: `required_tag=(tags[0] if tags else None)` silently drops a second `--tags` value. Either reject >1 (`ERROR: --tags supports one value`) or loop.
2. **Regex built by concatenation**: `"...['\"]" + tag + r"['\"]"` — fine for `integration`, but a tag with regex metacharacters would silently misbehave. Wrap with `re.escape(tag)`.
3. **4096-byte read window is silent**: a file whose `@Tags` sits past 4 KiB (long header/imports) would be silently dropped from the bin-pack safety net — i.e. a new integration test file that never runs and never warns. I verified all 73 current integration-tagged files match within the window and none use `@Tags(const [...])` (which the regex also would not match), so this is latent-only today — a `read()` of the whole file (test files are small) or a loud fallback would close it.

Related: `scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py` cannot validate the new manifest at all — `full_suite()` hard-codes the `/integration/` exclusion and there is no `--tags` pass-through, so the union/disjoint/no-extras invariant for `test_integration_shards.json` (verified manually for this PR) has no CI guard and will silently rot. Extending it with `--tags` (delegating to `shard_files.py`, as it already does) and wiring it into `guards` would make the manual check permanent.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicated dart-JSON span parser + no alarm for budgeted suites that stop running**

Two related points on the gate script:

1. **Second hand-rolled parser of the same format.** `parse_tests()` re-implements the `testStart`/`testDone` span logic of `scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py` (the docstring says "Same span logic"). The duration gate and the junit/rebalance pipeline must agree on durations forever; when someone fixes a parsing subtlety in one (e.g. retry semantics, group/hidden filtering), the other drifts. A tiny shared module (e.g. `scripts/_dart_json_spans.py` imported by both — both stay pure-stdlib) removes the drift class.

2. **A budgeted suite can silently exit the gate.** The check iterates suites *that ran*: a suite renamed, re-tagged, or dropped from the manifest keeps its dead baseline entry forever while its replacement shows up only on the "unbudgeted" visibility list — nobody is forced to act, and gated coverage quietly shrinks (the gate stays green with fewer gated suites). missing = sorted(set(baseline["suites"]) - set(suite_totals))
if missing:
    report.append(f"Budgeted suites NOT seen this run ({len(missing)}):")
    report.extend(f"  `{p}`" for p in missing)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 932
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/932
- **Title**: Add a test-duration budget gate on the PTY/CLI critical path (on top of #963's 3-shard leg)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/928-duration-gate` → `main`

- **Additions**: +403

- **Updated**: 2026-09-26T15:24:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #928 (Part 1; **rebased onto #963**, whose canonical 3-shard pty-integration + standing linux leg now owns Part 2.1 — this PR's original 2-shard manifest was dropped in the rebase, the gate sits on top of #963's structure).

## Delivered

**Part 1 — duration budget gate (blocking from day one)**
- `scripts/check_test_durations.py` (pure stdlib, mirrors `check_cli_coverage.py`): consumes the dart test JSON file-reporter the mac-leg integration shards now emit; **fails** when a suite total regresses >10% vs the baseline or a named per-test budget is breached; writes the **top-10 slowest tests into the GitHub job summary on every run**; **fails when a budgeted suite stops running** (renamed/retagged can't silently exit the ratchet). Suite total = sum of per-test spans, so sharding/concurrency changes don't move it.
- `scripts/test_duration_baseline.json` `{suites, per_test, _meta}` — seeded from a real measured no-key integration run (M-class arm64, `--tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), **×2 provisional headroom** (review round 1: local no-key hardware is not runner truth on `runner-pick` fa-m5/hosted; blocking stays on from day one), only for the 6 suites that fully execute without provider keys (124s → 248s budgeted). `_meta.provisional` pins the tighten-once-runner-junit-lands flow: `--update-baseline` on the first keyed leg's `integration-json` artifact in a reviewed PR (ratchet only tightens); raises are hand-edited reviewed PRs. Spawn-heavy PTY suites (fixed by #963's part 3) and all `llm` suites are **unbudgeted**: listed in every summary, gated the moment a reviewed PR budgets them.
- Ratchet is **structural**: `--update-baseline` refuses to RAISE an existing budget (exit 1), refuses sub-second env-skip totals (would poison a down-only ratchet with 0.0s floors), and **no workflow — scheduled or otherwise — ever invokes it**. `shard-rebalance.yml` / `coverage-gardener.yml` verified untouched. Budgets move only through reviewed PRs consuming the `junit-integration*` artifacts.
- Enforcement: **pty-coverage-gate** (#963's job, extended) runs #963's manifest assert + merged-coverage ratchet **and** the duration gate (mac-leg `integration-json-shard-*` only — the linux leg deliberately emits no json so the same suites aren't double-counted); `quality-gate`'s fail step checks `pty-coverage-gate` (`R_PTY_GATES`) → a breach red-blocks the required check, not just the needs edge. The nightly mac leg emits the same json+junit (retention 14d) and runs the gate **check-only** on the scheduled keyed run — that artifact is what completes the unbudgeted suites' budgets.
- Red-run evidence: junit convert + lcov format are `if: always()` steps decoupled from the failing `dart test` step — a red leg still ships json, junit, and merged coverage (the data red runs exist to produce).

**Before/after** — before: hosted-fallback leg wall **41.9 min** (nightly, hosted ubuntu — the case the issue cites); fa-m5 minis ~11-13 min. After: #963's 3 shards + linux leg own the wall-time cut; this PR's gate adds ~seconds (three stdlib parses). **The first SM-started CI run on this branch supplies the real after-number** — per fleet rules this PR dispatches no CI.

## Remaining (not in this PR, per scope)
- Part 2.2: data-driven shave/re-shard of the top offenders once the first keyed junit artifacts land.
- Budget tightening to runner truth (+20% of the first keyed `integration-json`) — one reviewed PR, command in `_meta`.
- Baseline coverage of the PTY-spawn-heavy suites (unblocked by #963's unique-CWD fix; budget them from the first keyed artifacts).

## Verification
- Gate script: 6-case synthetic battery (OK / suite-regression / per-test / update-lowers+adds / update-refuses-raise / budgeted-suite-did-not-run) — exit codes verified; run against the real 263-test/64-suite seed json → exit 0.
- Shared parser: `junit_from_dart_json.iter_test_spans` is the single span walk (gate imports it); junit output **md5-identical** pre/post refactor.
- Manifest parity: #963's `assert_shard_manifest.py` green on the rebased tree — union=78 == full integration suite, pairwise disjoint, no excluded leaks (25/28/25).
- Shard selector: 3/3 shards dry-run clean; `--tags` >1 value rejected; tag regex metachar-safe; full-file tag scan (superseded by #963's comment-stripping variant — kept theirs).
- Both workflows YAML-parse; `py_compile` clean on all touched scripts.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 932
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/932
- **Title**: Add a test-duration budget gate + 2-shard the PTY/CLI critical path
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/928-duration-gate` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +632
- **Deletions**: -38
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T19:23:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T19:23:09Z

## PR Description

Fixes #928 (Part 1 + Part 2.1; Part 3 and the data-driven shave are deliberately not here).

## Delivered

**Part 1 — duration budget gate (blocking from day one)**
- `scripts/check_test_durations.py` (pure stdlib, mirrors `check_cli_coverage.py`): consumes the dart test JSON file-reporter the integration legs now emit; **fails** when a suite total regresses >10% vs the baseline or a named per-test budget is breached; writes the **top-10 slowest tests into the GitHub job summary on every run** (plus unbudgeted-suite visibility). Suite total = sum of per-test spans, so sharding/concurrency changes don't move it.
- `scripts/test_duration_baseline.json` `{suites, per_test, _meta}` — seeded from a real measured no-key integration run (M-class arm64, `--tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), **+20% headroom**, only for the 6 suites that fully execute without provider keys (124s → 149s budgeted). Spawn-heavy PTY suites (blocked locally by the hardcoded `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd`, part 3.1) and all `llm` suites are **unbudgeted**: listed in every summary, gated the moment a reviewed PR budgets them.
- Ratchet is **structural**: `--update-baseline` refuses to RAISE an existing budget (exit 1), refuses sub-second env-skip totals (would poison a down-only ratchet with 0.0s floors), and **no workflow — scheduled or otherwise — ever invokes it**. `shard-rebalance.yml` / `coverage-gardener.yml` verified untouched. Budgets move only through reviewed PRs consuming the new `junit-integration*` artifacts.
- Enforcement: new **pty-coverage-gate** job (after the shards) runs the gate + the CLI coverage ratchet; `quality-gate` needs it → red-blocks the merge. The nightly leg emits the same json+junit (retention 14d) and runs the gate **check-only** on the scheduled keyed run — that artifact is what completes the unbudgeted suites' budgets.

**Part 2.1 — PTY/CLI leg sharded 2x**
- `scripts/test_integration_shards.json` (file-level, duration-balanced) + `shard_files.py --tags integration` (new flag: bin-packs uncovered *integration-tagged* files at runtime so a PR adding one never silently skips it; verified union/disjoint/no-extras for both shards). Matrix shards run `--file-reporter` + junit, upload json/junit/lcov artifacts; shard lcovs merge (union DA hits, NOT cat) before the coverage ratchet — a single shard's ratchet would false-regress.

**Before/after** — before: hosted-fallback leg wall **41.9 min** (nightly, hosted ubuntu — the case the issue cites); fa-m5 minis ~11-13 min recently (currently red on main for unrelated reasons). After: 2 parallel shards, test-phase spans split ~50/50 (estimated loads 3450s/3450s); **the first SM-started CI run on this branch supplies the real after-number** — per fleet rules this PR dispatches no CI.

## Remaining (not in this PR, per scope)
- Part 3 (product/test-harness code): `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp` unique CWD, dap hub port hygiene, explicit `--concurrency` tags, heavyweight-file splits. The `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` fix also unblocks local seeding of the remaining suites.
- Part 2.2: data-driven shave/re-shard of the top offenders once the first keyed junit artifacts land (candidates already named in the issue).

## Self-check evidence
- Gate script: 5-case synthetic battery (OK / suite-regression / per-test / update-lowers+adds / update-refuses-raise) all as expected, exit codes verified; run against the real 263-test/64-suite seed json → RESULT OK, exit 0.
- Ratchet poison guard: `--update-baseline` over the raw seed json budgets 15 meaningful suites and skips 58 sub-second env-skips (verified, no 0.0 floors land).
- Shard selector: both shards dry-run disjoint, union == manifest (73 files), zero bin-pack warnings, all targets exist.
- YAML: all touched workflows parse; `quality-gate`/`watchdog` needs-edges preserved.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…
